stories.headline: NextEra to buy Dominion in $67B all-stock deal, creating largest US regulated utility

key_facts.fact: NextEra Energy and Dominion Energy announced an all-stock merger on May 18, 2026, valued at about $66.8 billion — the largest utility acquisition in US history.
key_facts.excerpt: NextEra Energy Inc.'s $67 billion deal for rival Dominion Energy Inc., the largest utility acquisition in US history, suggests even the industry's biggest companies need to grow in order to accommodate the power demand driven by artificial intelligence.

key_facts.fact: The combined company will serve about 10 million utility customer accounts across Florida, Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina and own 110 gigawatts of generation.
key_facts.excerpt: The combined company will be more than 80% regulated, serve approximately 10 million utility customer accounts across Florida, Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina and own 110 gigawatts (GW) of generation across a broad mix of energy sources.

key_facts.fact: Dominion shareholders will receive 0.8138 NextEra shares per Dominion share, plus a one-time $360 million cash payment at closing.
key_facts.excerpt: Dominion shareholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 0.8138 shares of NextEra Energy for each share of Dominion that they own. Dominion stockholders will continue to receive Dominion's current quarterly dividend through closing, plus a one-time cash payment of $360m at closing.

key_facts.fact: NextEra and Dominion have data centers totaling about 130 gigawatts of electricity demand seeking to connect to the combined grid.
key_facts.excerpt: The deal will enable a swifter build-out of power infrastructure to deliver electricity to data centres proposing to connect to NextEra and Dominion, which total about 130 gigawatts of electricity demand, the companies' executives said.

key_facts.fact: The deal proposes $2.25 billion in bill credits for Dominion customers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina spread over two years post-close.
key_facts.excerpt: Additionally, the combined company is proposing $2.25 billion in bill credits for Dominion Energy's customers in Virginia, North Carolina and South Carolina spread over two years post-close.

key_facts.fact: US utilities and grid operators are expected to invest more than $1.1 trillion over the next five years on new generation and transmission projects to handle AI-driven demand.
key_facts.excerpt: Utilities and grid operators in the US are expected to invest more than $1.1 trillion over the next five years on new generation and transmission projects. That spending wave is increasing pressure to gain scale and financial heft.

key_facts.fact: The transaction was unanimously approved by both boards and is expected to close in 12 to 18 months, subject to FERC, NRC and state regulatory approvals.
key_facts.excerpt: The transaction has been unanimously approved by the boards of directors of both companies. The transaction is expected to close in 12 to 18 months, subject to customary closing conditions and approvals.

stories.headline: Standard Chartered to cut ~7,800 back-office roles by 2030 as it scales AI automation

key_facts.fact: Standard Chartered announced on May 18, 2026, that it will cut more than 15% of its corporate functions roles — about 7,800 jobs — by 2030 as it deploys AI and automation.
key_facts.excerpt: Standard Chartered on Tuesday announced it would cut more than 15% of its corporate functions roles by 2030, while setting higher medium-term profitability targets.

key_facts.fact: The cuts target back-office functions including HR, risk, compliance and supply chain; about 52,000 of StanChart's roughly 82,000 employees work in support roles per the 2025 annual report.
key_facts.excerpt: According to its 2025 annual report, corporate function roles include employees in human resources, corporate affairs and supply chain management. Of its roughly 82,000 employees, about 52,000 work in support roles.

key_facts.fact: CEO Bill Winters framed the reductions as 'replacing, in some cases, lower-value human capital with the financial capital and investment capital we're putting in.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'It's not cost cutting: it's replacing, in some cases, lower-value human capital with the financial capital and investment capital we're putting in,' he said.

key_facts.fact: The bank aims to raise income per employee by about 20% by 2028 and target a 15% return on tangible equity in 2028, rising to roughly 18% by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: The workforce reduction is part of the lender's efforts to raise income per employee by around 20% by 2028... The lender also aimed for a 15% return on tangible equity in 2028, up more than three percentage points from 2025, and targeted about 18% in 2030.

key_facts.fact: StanChart has major back-office operations in India, China, Malaysia and Poland; the company said it would try to redeploy some affected workers.
key_facts.excerpt: The company did not give details of where the roles would be cut. It has major back-office operations in India, China, Malaysia and Poland... The BBC understands that Standard Chartered aims to move some of the affected workers to other roles in the business.

key_facts.fact: The announcement was made at the bank's investor day in Hong Kong as part of CEO Bill Winters' new strategic plan.
key_facts.excerpt: The announcement, made by chief executive Bill Winters at an investor day in Hong Kong, singled out corporate functions including human resources, risk, and compliance as the primary areas for reduction.

stories.headline: Meta to lay off ~8,000 on May 20 while reassigning 7,000 employees into four new AI units

key_facts.fact: Meta will lay off about 10% of its workforce — roughly 8,000 employees — starting May 20, 2026, while also scrapping plans to fill 6,000 open roles.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg's company, which plans to cut its workforce by about 10% or about 8,000 jobs starting this week, is facing a new round of mass layoffs. The company also scrapped plans to fill 6,000 open roles.

key_facts.fact: Meta also told employees on Monday May 18 that about 7,000 workers would be reassigned to four newly created AI organizations, per an internal NYT-reported memo.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta informed employees on Monday that about 7,000 workers would be reassigned into four newly created AI organizations focused on building AI-powered products and tools, the New York Times reported, citing an internal memo.

key_facts.fact: The new AI units are Applied AI Engineering (autonomous AI agents), Agent Transformation Accelerator, Central Analytics, and Enterprise Solutions.
key_facts.excerpt: Applied AI Engineering (AAI) – focused on building autonomous AI agents. Agent Transformation Accelerator (ATA) – cross-functional teams to accelerate AI adoption. Central Analytics – measuring productivity and agent development. Enterprise Solutions – a new unit with details to be announced soon.

key_facts.fact: Meta raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance by up to $10 billion, taking the total to as high as $145 billion, largely directed at AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Last month, the company raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance by as much as $10 billion, bringing the total to as high as $145 billion.

key_facts.fact: Meta is eliminating thousands of managerial roles and instructing North American employees to work remotely on May 20, the day layoffs are scheduled.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta will eliminated thousands of managerial roles and also reassign 7,000 employees to new AI-focused initiatives... The company has already closed 6,000 open roles and instructed North American employees to work remotely on May 20.

key_facts.fact: Almost 110,000 layoffs have occurred at 137 tech companies so far in 2026, per Layoffs.fyi.
key_facts.excerpt: So far in 2026, there have been almost 110,000 layoffs at 137 tech companies.

stories.headline: Strategy buys 24,869 BTC for $2.01B, total stash hits 843,738 coins worth ~$65B

key_facts.fact: Strategy (MSTR) disclosed in a May 18 SEC 8-K filing that it bought 24,869 bitcoin between May 11 and 17 for about $2.01 billion at an average price of $80,985 per coin.
key_facts.excerpt: Strategy acquired 24,869 Bitcoin (BTC) for $2.01 billion between May 11 and 17, according Monday's 8-K filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. The purchases were made at an average price of $80,985 per BTC.

key_facts.fact: The acquisition brings Strategy's total holdings to 843,738 BTC, acquired for about $63.87 billion at an average cost basis of $75,700 per coin.
key_facts.excerpt: The company now holds 843,738 BTC, acquired for about $63.87 billion. At the time of publication, the holdings were valued at roughly $65.3 billion.

key_facts.fact: The purchases were funded almost entirely by selling 19.5 million shares of the company's high-yielding STRC preferred stock, raising about $1.9 billion, plus $84 million in common stock.
key_facts.excerpt: During the period from May 11 to May 17, Strategy raised $1.9 billion by selling approximately 19.5 million shares of its Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred Stock, and approximately $84 million through the sale of 430,344 shares of its Class A common stock.

key_facts.fact: The buy comes weeks after chairman Michael Saylor said on the company's early-May earnings call that Strategy will 'probably sell some bitcoin.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'Yeah, we'll probably sell some bitcoin,' Strategy chair Saylor said during the company's most recent earnings call in early May.

key_facts.fact: The acquisition marks a sharp escalation from Strategy's previous disclosed buy of just 535 BTC worth about $43 million earlier in May.
key_facts.excerpt: The move signals a sharp return to aggressive accumulation after Strategy's previous disclosed purchase totaled just 535 BTC worth around $43 million earlier this month.

stories.headline: Iran unveils 'Hormuz Safe' Bitcoin-backed shipping insurance for Strait of Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Iran's Ministry of Economy has launched 'Hormuz Safe,' a digital insurance platform that issues marine insurance policies for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz with payments settled in Bitcoin, per Fars News Agency reporting on May 18.
key_facts.excerpt: State-linked Fars News reported that Iran's economy ministry has been working on a plan to manage shipping through the Strait using marine insurance policies and financial responsibility certificates, with payments settled in bitcoin.

key_facts.fact: Officials project the platform could generate more than $10 billion in revenue for Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: Officials involved in the project estimate that the platform could eventually generate more than $10 billion in revenue for Iran, according to the report.

key_facts.fact: Policies would cover risks such as cargo inspection, detention, and confiscation — but exclude damages from weapon strikes.
key_facts.excerpt: The plan would start with insurance covering risks such as inspection, detention, and confiscation, excluding damages from weapon strikes.

key_facts.fact: About 20% of the world's crude oil and LNG supplies flowed through Hormuz before the US-Iran war began Feb. 28, 2026; the strait has been mostly closed since.
key_facts.excerpt: About 20% of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas supplies flowed through Hormuz prior to the war.

key_facts.fact: Any use of Hormuz Safe would create sanctions-compliance risk for shipowners, traders and insurers because payments would flow to Iranian state-linked entities.
key_facts.excerpt: Because payments to Iranian state-linked entities can trigger sanctions exposure, any use of Hormuz Safe would pose significant compliance risks for shipowners, traders and insurers, and the platform's operational status remains unverified.

key_facts.fact: Separately, Arkham reported Iran's largest crypto exchange Nobitex has processed more than $2.3 billion since 2023 via Tron and BNB Chain, including over $23 million since the Iran war started in February.
key_facts.excerpt: Arkham: Iran's largest crypto exchange, Nobitex, processed $2.3B+ since 2023 via Tron and BNB Chain, including $23M+ since the Iran war started in February (Reuters)

stories.headline: Trump postpones planned Tuesday Iran attack at request of Saudi, UAE, Qatar leaders

key_facts.fact: President Trump said on May 18 he was 'holding off' a scheduled Tuesday attack on Iran after the leaders of Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar asked for a pause to allow negotiations.
key_facts.excerpt: President Donald Trump said Monday that he will 'hold off' on a Tuesday plan to attack Iran, citing a request from the leaders of Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates as he said negotiations to end the war grow more 'serious.'

key_facts.fact: Trump instructed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine to be ready for a 'full, large scale assault of Iran, on a moment's notice' if no acceptable deal is reached.
key_facts.excerpt: The president said he told Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine that while Tuesday's attack is off, they should 'be prepared to go forward with a full, large scale assault of Iran, on a moment's notice, in the event that an acceptable Deal is not reached.'

key_facts.fact: Iran on May 18 conveyed its response to Washington's latest proposal through mediator Pakistan, per Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei told a press briefing on Monday that Tehran's response to the latest US proposal had been 'conveyed to the American side through mediator Pakistan.'

key_facts.fact: Washington's five-point proposal reportedly demands Iran keep only one nuclear site operational and transfer its highly enriched uranium stockpile to the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Iranian news agency Fars reported on Sunday that Washington had presented a five-point list, which made it clear the US would cease hostilities only when Tehran engages in formal peace negotiations. It also included a demand for Iran to keep only one nuclear site in operation and transfer its stockpile of highly enriched uranium to the US.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude rose more than 2% to settle at $112.10 a barrel on May 18, while WTI rose ~3% to $108.66, before easing in extended trading on news of the postponement.
key_facts.excerpt: International benchmark Brent crude futures rose more than 2% to close at $112.10 a barrel. U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures for June advanced about 3% to settle at $108.66 per barrel. But prices eased in extended trading with Brent dipping back below $110.

key_facts.fact: The IEA warned global oil inventories are 'depleting at a record pace' with cumulative supply losses from Gulf producers already exceeding 1 billion barrels and more than 14 mb/d shut in.
key_facts.excerpt: With Hormuz tanker traffic still restricted, cumulative supply losses from Gulf producers already exceed 1 billion barrels with more than 14 mb/d of oil now shut in, an unprecedented supply shock.

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical 'Magnifica Humanitas' on AI to release May 25

key_facts.fact: The Vatican announced on May 18 that Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical letter, 'Magnifica Humanitas,' on preserving the human person in the age of AI, will be released May 25, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical, Magnifica humanitas, on preserving the human person in the age of artificial intelligence, will be released on May 25. A presentation event with the Pope and various speakers is scheduled for the same day at the Vatican.

key_facts.fact: The Pope signed the encyclical on May 15, the 135th anniversary of Pope Leo XIII's encyclical Rerum Novarum that responded to the Industrial Revolution.
key_facts.excerpt: It bears the Pope's signature dated May 15th, 135th anniversary of the publication of Pope Leo XIII's encyclical Rerum novarum.

key_facts.fact: Breaking with precedent, Pope Leo XIV — the first American-born pope — will personally speak at the presentation and deliver a final blessing; Anthropic co-founder Jared Olah-tied theologian among the announced speakers.
key_facts.excerpt: Breaking with precedent, the American-born pope will speak at the presentation of the text and provide a final blessing, the Vatican said.

key_facts.fact: Speakers at the Synod Hall presentation will include Cardinal Prefect of the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, Cardinal Michael Czerny SJ, an Anthropic co-founder and head of research, and Catholic theologian Lokadie Lushombo.
key_facts.excerpt: Cardinal, Prefect of the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith; Cardinal Michael Czerny, S.J... a theologian and co-founder of Anthropic (USA) and head of research; Lokadie Lushombo, professor of political theology and Catholic Theology / Santa Clara

key_facts.fact: The encyclical follows the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith's January 2025 doctrinal note 'Antiqua et Nova,' which argued AI must remain under human moral oversight and warned of civilization-scale risks.
key_facts.excerpt: On January 28, 2025, the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith issued Antiqua et Nova, a 30-page doctrinal note on the relationship between artificial intelligence and human intelligence... it argued that artificial intelligence is a product of human intelligence, not a rival form of it, and insisted that AI systems must remain under human moral oversight.
